newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks edge ahead in light trade.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks edge ahead in light trade.

text.p: Caracas stocks edged ahead in light trade but were little moved by the Central Bank's decision to modify Venezuela's floating exchange rate bands system, traders said.
The Central Bank said Sunday the bolivar's central parity, to be set at 472 per dollar on Jan 2, would depreciate by 1.32 percent per month within bands set 7.5 percent either side.
"All one saw today was some re-jigging of portfolios and some cross-trades," said Merinvest analyst Roberto Isasi. "But everything points to a lot of activity next quarter."
The market's 19-share index closed up 0.25 percent at 6,623.48 as 19 shares rose, 12 fell and six closed flat.
Volume was boosted to 36.07 million shares, worth 1.8 billion bolivars ($3.8 million), as 13 million Corimon Type B shares cross-traded. The stock closed up 0.2 bolivars at 8.95.
With most Caracas businesses shut for the New Year holiday, brokers said trading would pick up after the second week of January.
